source: KC Performances Space (twelve venue calendars, venue-primary per David's rule); converted by scripts/performances-feed-builder.mjs

items.title: The Pigeon Gets a Big Time Holiday Extravaganza!
items.timeText: Matinees and evenings, times vary by date
items.preview: Mo Willems' Pigeon tries to run the holidays single-handedly and learns he cannot do it alone. Silly songs and big laughs for young kids and their grown-ups.

items.title: Sherlock Holmes and the Adventure of the Elusive Ear
items.preview: Holmes and Watson team up with Irene Adler and Oscar Wilde to outwit Moriarty's daughter in a fast, funny mystery. Classic Holmes with witty banter and a comic twist, no prior Holmes knowledge needed.

items.title: Always... Patsy Cline
items.timeText: Dinner theatre: evening and matinee seatings
items.preview: Dinner-theatre favorite: superfan Louise tells how she met Patsy Cline, woven through 27 songs including 'Crazy,' 'I Fall to Pieces' and 'Walkin' After Midnight,' all over dinner.

items.title: A Christmas Carol
items.timeText: Matinees and evenings, times vary by date
items.preview: KC Rep's beloved holiday tradition: Ebenezer Scrooge, three ghosts and a big-hearted redemption story. The classic Dickens tale staged for the whole family.

items.title: Tim Gaither
items.preview: KC native headliner known for clean, observational stories about family and growing up in Kansas. A homecoming set to open the holiday week.

items.title: A Thanksgiving Dinner Party
items.preview: Improv comedy staged like an awkward family Thanksgiving dinner, arguments, secrets and all, made up on the spot.

items.title: April Macie
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Fearless, adults-only headliner from the Howard Stern Show and Last Comic Standing, known for unfiltered sets on dating, sex and double standards.

items.title: Godfrey
items.preview: High-energy impressionist and actor (Zoolander, Soul Plane) famous for spot-on voices and riffs on race, pop culture and everyday absurdity.

items.title: The Bird Comedy Show
items.preview: The Bird's house troupe does fast improv and sketch built from your suggestions. The best intro to the Crossroads comedy scene if you have never been.

items.title: The All-Ages Truck Noises Show!
items.preview: All-ages sketch and improv where the cast builds scenes out of silly sounds, truck noises very much included. A good first comedy show for families.

items.title: The Phantom of the Opera
items.preview: Andrew Lloyd Webber's gothic blockbuster: a masked composer haunts the Paris Opera and falls for young singer Christine. The new touring production with the famous chandelier and 'The Music of the Night.'

items.title: Ron Funches
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: The gentle giant of comedy, voice of Cooper in Trolls and a Bob's Burgers regular, with a soft delivery and joyful, weird takes on fatherhood, gaming and kindness. Lovably offbeat.

items.title: Training Center Fall 2026 Showcase
items.preview: Students from The Bird's improv classes show what they have learned. A raw, supportive graduation show that is often surprisingly funny.

items.title: Chris Porter
items.preview: Kansas-bred comic from Last Comic Standing, known for 'Ugly and Angry' and 'A Man From Kansas.' Dry, self-deprecating takes on getting older and Midwest life.

items.title: Free First Friday Comedy
items.preview: Free sampler of improv, sketch and stand-up for First Friday in the Crossroads. A low-risk way to try The Bird for the first time.

items.title: Gary Owen
items.preview: Longtime crowd favorite from BET's ComicView and Think Like a Man, on the No Hard Feelings Tour: storytelling sets on family, marriage and race.

items.title: Robby Hoffman
items.preview: Emmy-winning writer for Workin' Moms and Hacks with brutally honest, deadpan stand-up on identity and family. A cult favorite worth discovering live.

items.title: The Secret Show
items.preview: The lineup stays secret until showtime: expect surprise drop-ins and comics testing brand-new material late on a Friday.

items.title: Ari Matti
items.preview: Estonian comic who tours the world in English with sharp, dark observational sets and a huge online following for crowd work.

items.title: Dusty Slay
items.preview: Nashville comic in the trucker hat known for 'We're having a good time' and dry stories about trailer parks, odd jobs and small-town life, as seen on Netflix and The Tonight Show.

items.title: Anti-Hero: Revenge of the Swifties
items.preview: World premiere comedy about Taylor Swift fans who decide to take justice into their own hands. A playful riff on fandom, friendship and revenge, fun whether or not you are a Swiftie.

items.title: Nate Jackson
items.preview: Big, crowd-working headliner seen on Netflix and Wild 'N Out, on his Big Dog tour. Playful roasts and audience interaction are a big part of the show.

items.title: Nicole Burch
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Storyteller comic known for brutally funny tales about dating disasters and single-mom life. A one-night set.

items.title: Connor Ratliff presents The Acting Class
items.preview: Connor Ratliff of The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel and The George Lucas Talk Show leads a fake-serious acting class that spirals into improv comedy.

items.title: Jessica Kirson
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Powerhouse crowd-worker famous for characters, voices and rapid-fire energy. A very interactive show, expect her to talk to the front rows.

items.title: The Big Gay Holiday Extravaganza!
items.preview: A queer holiday variety blowout of sketch, improv and music, big festive energy to close out the season.

items.title: Rene Vaca
items.preview: Fast-rising Latino headliner with high-energy sets on family and culture, joined by Texas rapper That Mexican OT for a comedy and music night.

items.title: Rob Anderson
items.preview: Work-in-progress hour from the singer-comedian behind the viral 'Gay Science' songs. Musical comedy and pop-culture bits he is testing live.

items.title: Mel Mitchell
items.preview: Rising stand-up with sharp, personal sets on dating, family and millennial life. A one-night club set.

items.title: David Koechner
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: You know him as Todd Packer on The Office and Champ Kind in Anchorman. A Kansas City area native doing character-driven stand-up close to home.

items.title: Marcus D. Wiley
items.preview: Clean, church-friendly headliner and radio host known for character bits like Bishop Secular. Big storytelling without going blue.

items.title: The Anarchy Fun Time Show
items.preview: Anything-goes improv where the cast breaks its own rules. Messier and looser than the regular Bird show, in a fun way.

items.title: The Improv Show
items.preview: Straight-up late-night improv: scenes and games invented live from audience prompts by Bird players.

items.title: Bingo Loco
items.preview: Not quiet bingo: a rave-style bingo party with DJs, confetti, dance-offs and prizes. Loud, participatory and very silly.

items.title: The Bird Musical Comedy Show
items.preview: Improv plus songs made up on the spot, full musical numbers invented from a single audience suggestion.

items.title: Liz Blanc
items.preview: Quick-witted club comic with sets on work, relationships and getting older. An early Sunday show.

items.title: Alfred Kainga
items.preview: Zimbabwe-born, Texas-based comic with high-energy stories about immigrating to the US, family and culture clash.

items.title: Damon Williams
items.preview: Chicago veteran of ComicView and The Tom Joyner Morning Show with smooth, observational sets on family and everyday life, headlining New Year's Eve.

items.title: New Year's Eve at The Bird
items.preview: Improv and sketch to ring in the New Year in the Crossroads, a smaller, sillier alternative to a big club New Year's Eve.

items.title: The Bodyguard
items.preview: Musical built around Whitney Houston's hits: a former Secret Service agent is hired to protect pop star Rachel Marron from a stalker, and romance complicates the job. Includes 'I Will Always Love You.'

items.title: Emma Willmann
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Netflix and Crazy Ex-Girlfriend comic with fast, confessional sets on small-town roots, dating and ADHD.

items.title: Shapel Lacey
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Former competitive cheerleader turned comic with physical, high-energy stories about identity, family and growing up in Arizona.

items.title: Marlon Wayans
items.preview: Wayans family star of White Chicks, Scary Movie and In Living Color doing straight stand-up: wild impressions, family stories and celebrity riffs.

items.title: Todd Barry
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Master of deadpan: very dry, very quiet, devastatingly funny one-liners delivered at low volume. A cult favorite for 30 years.

items.title: Marc Maron
items.preview: The WTF podcast legend and GLOW actor with a confessional, neurotic hour on aging, cats, grief and trying to be a person. Smart, raw stand-up.

items.title: Six The Musical
items.preview: Henry VIII's six wives reclaim their stories as a pop concert, each singing her case for who had it worst. About 80 minutes with no intermission, all big pop numbers.

items.title: Jacked! A Beanstalk Remix
items.preview: Jack and the Beanstalk remixed with hip-hop and beatboxing and a modern lesson about greed and community. Best for ages 10 and up who like fairy tales with a beat.

items.title: Dave Hill
items.venue: The Comedy Club of Kansas City
items.preview: Comic, musician and This American Life contributor mixing absurd stand-up with shredding guitar bits. Delightfully weird.

items.title: Boeing Boeing
items.preview: Classic 1960s farce with dinner: a Paris bachelor juggles three flight-attendant fiancees until faster jets and bad weather wreck his perfect timetable. Doors slam and identities swap.

items.title: Job
items.preview: Tense two-person thriller: a crisis-hotline worker unravels during a job interview that turns into an interrogation. Short, intense and twisty, it keeps you guessing to the end.
